competitors.name: Ethyco (data center commissioning, warranty-phase support)
competitors.what_they_do: Data center Cx firm that sells warranty-phase support: a 10-month pre-expiry warranty review, deferred-items tracking, post-occupancy observation and warranty deficiency documentation. This is the closest thing to the audit half of the idea. It is not idle-hall-specific, has no contingency model that I could find, and does not negotiate OEM start-date deferrals. Any Cx firm could add the same line.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Small boutique consultancy; no funding data found

competitors.name: Anyset AI (agentic closeout / warranty tracking)
competitors.what_they_do: AI agents that classify closeout submittals, O&Ms and warranties, cross-check warranty duration against spec, and run 'warranty tracking' from first submittal to final claim. Pulls from Procore, Autodesk and Trimble. General construction, not data-center-specific. It extracts documents and does not inspect equipment or file OEM claims.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Venture-backed startup; round size not disclosed in anything I found

competitors.name: Nomic (AEC document AI, closeout)
competitors.what_they_do: Domain-specific AI that parses drawings, specs and closeout packages, extracts warranty and O&M requirements, and builds searchable post-turnover repositories. Sells to owners and designers as a horizontal platform. This is the doc-extraction layer the idea depends on, so it is commoditizing.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Funded AEC AI company (Crunchbase profile exists); amount not verified

competitors.name: Trane delayed start-up warranty (OEM rider)
competitors.what_they_do: Trane sells an optional Delayed Start-up Warranty that postpones the first-year parts warranty start when startup is more than 6 months after shipment. Standard CenTraVac terms are 12 months from startup or 18 months from shipment, whichever is earlier. This weakens the idea's claim that nobody can defer the clock, because OEMs already package the fix as a product.

competitors.name: Cummins and Eaton standard warranty terms
competitors.what_they_do: Cummins stationary gensets: warranty starts at startup or 18 months after factory ship, whichever is sooner. Eaton 93E UPS: 12 months from startup or 18 from shipment. See https://www.eaton.com/us/en/catalog/services/startup--warranty-and-support-overview/eaton-93e-ups-startup--warranty-and-support-overview.html. These terms confirm the core premise: an outer-limit clock runs from shipment regardless of load.

competitors.name: SGS / vHive / SkySpecs / WindGuard end-of-warranty inspections (wind analog)
competitors.what_they_do: Established, paid service in wind energy: independent inspection 6-12 months before OEM warranty expiry to surface defects and file claims, with owners buying it because OEMs reject claims filed after expiry. Proves the business pattern and the buyer behavior. Nobody has ported it to data center power and cooling that I could find.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Multiple established vendors (SGS is a global inspection major)

competitors.name: Sinovoltaics (PV and BESS warranty claim management)
competitors.what_they_do: Technical warranty claim management for solar PV and battery storage: evidence, documentation, OEM dispute support. Closest 'claims for hire' analog in a neighboring asset class. Pricing model not disclosed.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Established Hong Kong-based service firm; no funding data

competitors.name: TWAICE Warranty Manager (BESS)
competitors.what_they_do: Analytics software that tracks battery warranty conditions and performance against OEM terms for storage owners. Software-only and battery-only.

competitors.name: Equipment Warranty Log
competitors.what_they_do: AI extraction of warranty packets and expiry dates plus maintenance scheduling, $18.99/month flat. Shows the doc-to-ledger step is already a cheap SaaS commodity for facilities teams. No claim filing.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Tiny SaaS; price point is the signal

competitors.name: CxPlanner and Bluerithm (data center commissioning software)
competitors.what_they_do: Purpose-built commissioning, punch-list and issue tracking for data center L1-L5 Cx, with AI agents. Owns the punch-list and deferred-items data during construction. Warranty ledger and claims are not named features, but adding them is a small step. Bluerithm: https://bluerithm.com/the-best-commissioning-software-for-data-centers/
competitors.scale_or_funding: Funded Cx SaaS; amounts not verified

competitors.name: Device42 / Sunbird / NetZoom DCIM warranty tracking
competitors.what_they_do: DCIM asset records with warranty expiry dates and alerts, mostly for IT gear (servers) via vendor APIs. Weak on facility-side MEP (gensets, chillers, switchgear) with real voiding conditions.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Established DCIM vendors (Sunbird, Device42 under Freshworks)

competitors.name: Warranty Consulting Services (WCS)
competitors.what_they_do: Warranty administration and claim recovery for heavy-equipment dealers, 150+ manufacturers, since 1997. Shows warranty claim recovery is a viable outsourced business. Serves the dealer side, not asset owners, and not data centers.

competitors.name: Aggreko and Sunbelt Solomon (load bank commissioning and rental)
competitors.what_they_do: Rent and run load banks for data center commissioning and IST. They already own the physical capability that the 'load-dependent defect inspection' step needs. Potential partners, or competitors if they package a warranty-expiry test. Sunbelt Solomon: https://sunbeltsolomon.com/data-center-commissioning-101-validating-critical-power-systems-with-load-banks/
competitors.scale_or_funding: Large established rental and services companies

white_space: Nobody I found combines all of these for data center MEP: (1) a serial-number-level clock ledger built for idle or deferred-start halls, (2) a pre-expiry loaded stress test using the idle capacity, (3) OEM claim filing and start-date deferral negotiation, and (4) success-fee or fixed-fee pricing sold to the owner or its lender. The pieces exist separately. Anyset and Nomic do doc extraction. Ethyco-style Cx firms do a 10-month warranty review. Wind and solar have end-of-warranty inspection and claims firms. OEMs sell delayed-start riders. Load-bank vendors have the hardware. Data center power and cooling MEP has no dedicated end-of-warranty claims specialist that I could find. Three structural weaknesses limit the wedge. (a) The clocks mostly start at OEM startup, and startup plus IST with load banks already loads equipment in Cx, so the 'idle for 12+ months' exposure is narrower than the pitch implies. It mainly hits gear started early or shipped more than 18 months before use. (b) 'Recovered value' is really avoided repair cost. It is hard to measure and easy for OEMs to dispute, and OEMs can deny on storage or light-load grounds (wet stacking is explicitly excluded, https://cliffordpower.com/wet-stacking-why-its-important-to-load-bank-your-diesel-generator/). A pure 25-30% contingency model will be hard to collect. (c) Documents are the commodity step, so the moat has to be inspection plus OEM leverage, not the LLM pipeline.
evidence_of_demand: Indirect only. I found no direct customer complaints, RFPs, or forum threads saying a hall's warranty lapsed while idle. Supporting evidence, weakest to strongest: (1) OEM terms create the shipment-based outer limit: Cummins (18 months from ship) https://www.cummins.com/sites/default/files/2018-08/A042E778.pdf, Eaton (18 months from ship) https://www.eaton.com/us/en/catalog/services/startup--warranty-and-support-overview/eaton-93e-ups-startup--warranty-and-support-overview.html, Trane (12 months from startup or 18 from ship, with a paid delayed-start rider) https://www.trane.com/commercial/north-america/us/en/services/operate-maintain-repair/hvac-system-management/extended-warranty.html. That OEMs sell a delayed-start rider shows the problem is real and priced. (2) Law firm guidance tells developers to make contractor warranties commence no earlier than Tier Certification, which shows owners think about warranty timing: https://www.womblebonddickinson.com/us/insights/alerts/critical-performance-guarantees-data-center-construction-contracts-and-risk. (3) Data center Cx firms already sell a 10-month pre-expiry warranty review, so owners pay for this kind of service: https://www.ethyco.com/services.html. (4) Wind energy shows a mature paid market for end-of-warranty inspections, because OEMs reject claims filed after expiry: https://www.sgs.com/en-us/services/end-of-warranty-inspection and https://skyspecs.com/blog/end-of-warranty-inspections/. (5) Fleet warranty recovery is a known leak: spreadsheet tracking recovers only ~15-22% of owed warranty value (https://fleetrabbit.com/industry/construction-management-system/construction-equipment-warranty-tracking-oem-claims), and outsourced warranty administration is an established business (https://www.warrantyconsultants.com/). (6) Idle-capital cost is large: $15-40M financing charges on a $500M build sitting idle (https://exto360.com/the-30-150m-problem-why-commissioning-delays-are-the-biggest-risk-in-data-center-construction/), which makes owners attentive but is a schedule pain, not a warranty pain. The 'why now' premise is contested. Reports say ~half of 2026 US capacity is not under construction (https://www.theregister.com/on-prem/2026/06/17/only-half-of-us-datacenter-capacity-planned-for-2026-is-actually-under-construction/5257781), but SemiAnalysis argues most of that is phantom announcements and shows no evidence of energized-but-empty halls (https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/stop-saying-half-of-2026-us-datacenter). The target population of 'commissioned 6-14 months ago and unloaded' is unproven and must be validated with real owners.
sharper_angle: Drop the generic 'warranty recovery audit' and the 25-30% contingency lead. Position it as an end-of-warranty load-test sprint for energized-but-underloaded halls, the wind end-of-warranty inspection model ported to data center MEP. Product: 6-9 months before each OEM clock expires, rent load banks (Aggreko/Sunbelt-type partners) and use the hall's idle capacity to run staged loaded tests on gensets (avoiding wet-stacking exclusions), UPS/battery, chillers/CDUs and breakers while the OEM is still liable. Then file claims with OEM-grade evidence and negotiate deferral or extension riders (Trane-style delayed-start warranty). Lead with a fixed-fee audit ($15-40K) and add a success fee only on defects the test actually surfaces. Sell to whoever needs certainty on a dated event: the owner's lender or technical advisor, ABS or refinancing due diligence, and buyers of stabilized powered-shell assets. Put the document-extraction pipeline behind the scenes as an internal tool, since Anyset, Nomic and Equipment Warranty Log are commoditizing it. Partner with, or pre-empt, Cx firms like Ethyco rather than compete with them, and add a PO-stage clause pack plus deferred-start rider brokerage as a cheap top-of-funnel. Before building, do the one check the research could not complete: find 5-10 owners with halls actually energized and idle 8-14 months, and confirm from their OEM terms and startup dates that clocks are running out on unloaded equipment.
